definition: LG ThinQ (pronounced as "think-cue"; sometimes known as LG webOS) is a smart home and artificial intelligence brand launched by LG Electronics in 2017, featuring products that are equipped with voice control and artificial intelligence technology.
details: The brand was originally launched for home appliances and consumer electronics, such as televisions, smart home devices, mobile devices, refrigerators, air conditioners and related services. The name was first used in 2011 for LG's THINQ-branded smart appliances, which were introduced at the Consumer Electronics Show in Las Vegas. In December 2017, LG announced ThinQ as a unified brand for artificial intelligence-enabled home appliances, consumer electronics and services.In February 2018, LG announced the LG V30S ThinQ, which is the first phone to have the "ThinQ" branding.

explainer.lead: LG ThinQ is a smart home and AI brand launched by LG Electronics in 2017, covering products with voice control and AI technology. It matters as an example of AI branding applied across appliances and consumer electronics.

tiers.eli5: A label LG puts on fridges, TVs and other devices that can understand voice commands and act smartly.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers building connected home products target the ThinQ brand's appliance, TV and mobile categories when integrating voice control. A pitfall is that the ThinQ name spans many product generations, so its capabilities differ by device.
tiers.paperLevel: No formal definition; it is a product brand for AI-enabled home appliances, consumer electronics and services, announced as a unified brand in December 2017.

explainer.example: The name first appeared in 2011 on THINQ-branded smart appliances shown at CES in Las Vegas, before the 2017 unified launch.
